abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel paradigm shift in distributed sensing by proposing a completely decentralized collaborative perception framework that eliminates reliance on centralized coordination nodes, which have traditionally been performance bottlenecks in sensor networks. Unlike conventional approaches that require hierarchical data aggregation, our framework employs a gossip-based consensus mechanism where individual sensor nodes exchange probabilistic belief states to achieve network-wide situational awareness. We formulate this problem within a distributed optimization framework and rigorously prove that our algorithm converges to the optimal maximum a posteriori estimate under mild assumptions regarding communication reliability and network connectivity. The theoretical analysis establishes that the convergence rate scales polylogarithmically with network diameter, enabling scalability to large-scale deployments. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the proposed paradigm exhibits inherent resilience to node failures and Byzantine faults, as consensus emerges from local interactions rather than depending on critical infrastructure. Simulation results across diverse network topologies validate our theoretical findings and reveal that the decentralized approach achieves comparable accuracy to centralized methods while reducing communication overhead by approximately 60%. This work fundamentally reimagines the architecture of distributed sensing systems and opens new research directions for self-organizing sensor networks in applications ranging from environmental monitoring to smart infrastructure management.

Energy consumption in wireless sensor networks remains a critical challenge that fundamentally limits deployment longevity, particularly for battery-powered devices performing continuous environmental monitoring. This paper presents a game-theoretic framework for optimizing sensing duty cycles that significantly improves upon existing approaches by explicitly modeling the strategic interactions among heterogeneous sensor nodes competing for shared communication resources. We formulate the sensing scheduling problem as a non-cooperative game where each node selects its active/sleep intervals to maximize individual utility while contributing to network coverage requirements. Our analysis reveals that the naive best-response dynamics converge slowly and may oscillate, motivating the introduction of a modified log-linear learning algorithm that guarantees convergence to Nash equilibrium in polynomial time. Rigorous theoretical bounds demonstrate that the achieved equilibrium configuration attains at least 85% of the social optimal welfare, representing a substantial improvement over prior learning algorithms with weaker performance guarantees. Extensive numerical experiments across varying network densities and traffic loads confirm that our approach reduces overall energy consumption by 28-35% compared to state-of-the-art duty cycling protocols while maintaining acceptable data delivery latency. The proposed framework provides principled guidance for designing energy-efficient sensing strategies in Internet of Things deployments where computational resources at individual nodes are limited.

This paper presents SensorMesh, a novel middleware architecture designed to address the fundamental mismatch between traditional sensor network protocols and the heterogeneous, dynamic nature of modern Internet of Things deployments. Existing middleware solutions typically assume homogeneous sensor capabilities and static network topologies, making them inadequate for scenarios involving diverse devices, varying quality of service requirements, and frequent topology changes. SensorMesh introduces a unified abstraction layer that exposes sensor resources as composable microservices, enabling dynamic composition of sensing pipelines across heterogeneous devices. The architecture incorporates a distributed registry that maintains real-time device capability advertisements and supports intelligent service discovery based on application requirements. We implement SensorMesh on commodity hardware and validate its effectiveness through deployment in two application domains: smart building management integrating temperature, occupancy, and air quality sensors, and precision agriculture coordinating soil moisture, light, and weather sensors. Our system demonstrates seamless interoperability among devices from multiple manufacturers without requiring application-specific modifications. Performance evaluation reveals that SensorMesh reduces application development time by 60% compared to direct sensor programming while incurring only 3-5% overhead in data acquisition latency. This work establishes a new architectural pattern for sensor data processing in IoT ecosystems that prioritizes flexibility and interoperability.

Indoor localization systems based on wireless sensor networks have gained substantial attention for applications including asset tracking, emergency response, and assisted living, yet achieving centimeter-level accuracy with practical deployment constraints remains challenging. This paper introduces a multi-modal fusion localization system that significantly improves positioning accuracy by synergistically combining received signal strength indicators, channel state information, and inertial measurement data through an adaptive extended Kalman filter framework. Unlike prior fusion approaches that rely on static weighting schemes, our system employs online learned confidence weights that adapt to environmental dynamics and device-specific characteristics. We implement the complete localization pipeline on low-power sensor nodes equipped with commodity Wi-Fi radios and accelerometer-gyroscope modules, enabling practical deployment without specialized infrastructure. Extensive field testing across three diverse indoor environments—including office spaces, warehouses, and hospital corridors—demonstrates that our system achieves median localization errors of 23 centimeters, representing a 42% improvement over the best existing approach in our test scenarios. The system maintains robust performance despite environmental variations caused by human movement and furniture reconfiguration. Power consumption analysis confirms that the proposed approach operates within the constraints of battery-powered sensor nodes for continuous tracking applications, with an average current draw of 12 mA during active localization.
